name: Joseph Schooling
method: Muse Spark web search (3 calls) for leads; every fact re-read from the cited page by the agent. corroborated = two or more independent sources.

facts.text: His parents met at a Pesta Sukan softball tournament in Penang: May Yim played for Perak, Colin Schooling for Singapore's Pirates team.

sources.label: Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)

facts.text: Colin and May married in 1983.

sources.label: Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)
Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling

facts.text: After several miscarriages (Tatler says three), Joseph was born 12 years after the wedding, when May was 40.
facts.quote: He was a miracle - and an amazingly easy baby!
facts.speaker: May Schooling

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling
Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)

facts.text: Born 16 June 1995 in Singapore, the couple's only child.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Joseph Schooling
Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)

facts.text: May grew up poor in Ipoh, Perak, getting new clothes only at Chinese New Year, and worked as a chartered accountant; Colin was a businessman.

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling
The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)

facts.text: Colin was a sportsman first: hurdles and water polo at Raffles Institution, then national softball.

sources.label: Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)

facts.text: May could not swim beyond a doggy paddle; Joseph was a fearless 'water baby', so she made sure he learnt to be water-safe.
facts.quote: I didn't start swimming to win the Olympics. It was just to be safe in the water.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling (SwimSwam, 2025)

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling
SwimSwam Magazine, 2025, 'Joseph Schooling: Singapore's hero'

facts.text: Filipina helper Yolanda 'Auntie Yolly' Pascual joined the household in 1997; he has called her a 'second mum' and, back home, still asked her for massages.
facts.quote: He'll always say 'I want to be No. 1'.
facts.speaker: Yolanda Pascual

sources.label: The Sunday Times (Jean Iau), 14 Aug 2016, on domestic helper Yolanda Pascual (reprint)

facts.text: At three he was taught by his first coach, Vincent Poon, at Tanah Merah Country Club; over four years Poon pitted him against older, bigger boys.
facts.quote: He worked really hard and listened.
facts.speaker: Vincent Poon

sources.label: The Sunday Times (Jean Iau), 14 Aug 2016, 'Schooling learnt to be fearless from first coach Vincent Poon' (reprint)

facts.text: Once he refused to race a much taller boy in a 50 m butterfly; Poon told him size mattered less than being fearless, and he won.
facts.quote: Vincent inculcated that hunger in him to win.
facts.speaker: Colin Schooling

sources.label: The Sunday Times (Jean Iau), 14 Aug 2016, 'Schooling learnt to be fearless from first coach Vincent Poon' (reprint)

facts.text: His Olympic obsession began after meeting his grand-uncle Lloyd Valberg, Singapore's first Olympian (London 1948).

sources.label: The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)
Wikipedia: Joseph Schooling

facts.text: He played golf with his father, went on bowling trips to Kuala Lumpur, and ate with him at the Lagoon hawker centre at East Coast Park.

sources.label: Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)

facts.text: On holidays with his mother's family in Ipoh he still swam, sometimes from 5am, at the city council pool and the family's pool.
facts.quote: Even when he was here on holiday, he would go swimming as early as 5am.
facts.speaker: Yim Kam Ling, his aunt

sources.label: The Straits Times, 15 Aug 2016, 'Aunt in Ipoh says her heart is bursting with joy' (reprint)

facts.text: His mother says she simply played every sport with him; friends describe a boy who could not stand losing.
facts.quote: He hates to lose more than he loves to win.
facts.speaker: May Schooling

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling
The Sunday Times (Jean Iau), 14 Aug 2016, 'Friends tell of swimmer's competitive streak' (reprint)

facts.text: Aged 13 and bespectacled, he asked Michael Phelps for a photo when the US team trained in Singapore before Beijing; the two later recalled chasing monkeys that stole energy bars from the pool deck at the Singapore Island Country Club.

sources.label: ESPN (Julian Linden), 14 Aug 2016, 'How Joseph Schooling and tiny Singapore rocked Rio'
The Sunday Times (May Chen, Rio), 14 Aug 2016, 'His first steps as Olympic victor' (reprint)

facts.text: At 14 he pleaded to go to the Bolles School in Florida; his mother first said no.
facts.quote: Mum, if I want to go to the Olympics, you have to let me go
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling, as his mother recalls

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling
The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)

facts.text: The first year apart was the hardest: he was homesick and not used to independence.
facts.quote: I cried all the time. He did too.
facts.speaker: May Schooling

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling
The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)

facts.text: He later admitted he was hard to coach at first.
facts.quote: I wasn't the easiest guy to train. I didn't want to be there.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling (2016)

sources.label: The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)

facts.text: Colin's one request to coach Sergio Lopez when Joseph arrived in Florida was about character, not times.
facts.quote: Sergio, I want my son to be a gentleman, to be a good person
facts.speaker: Colin Schooling, as Lopez recalls

sources.label: ESPN, 30 Mar 2020, 'Is Joseph Schooling ready for more gold?'

facts.text: His parents took turns living with him in the US for months at a time; the three of them averaged about three weeks a year together.

sources.label: The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)
Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling

facts.text: The family spent about US$1 million (S$1.35 million) on his training and education; they mortgaged their home, sold a house in Perth and cashed out an endowment plan.
facts.quote: using up all our reserves and having to budget like crazy
facts.speaker: May Schooling

sources.label: The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)
Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling
Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)

facts.text: May still wore Marks & Spencer trousers she had bought in her working days in 1990.

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling

facts.text: Colin, a handyman, built swimming contraptions for his son and kept thick folders of statistics and research.

sources.label: Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)

facts.text: At London 2012, aged 17, officials rejected his cap and goggles minutes before his 200 m butterfly heat; he swam 1:59.18 and finished 26th of 37.
facts.quote: I'm only 17 and I have a long way to go.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling

sources.label: RED SPORTS, 2 Aug 2012, London 2012 200 m butterfly heat

facts.text: An online comment, 'Singapore will never have an Olympic champion', stayed with him.
facts.quote: At least put yourself out there.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling

sources.label: SwimSwam Magazine, 2025, 'Joseph Schooling: Singapore's hero'

facts.text: He took up a place at the University of Texas, training under Eddie Reese, after Singapore deferred his National Service.

sources.label: ESPN (Julian Linden), 14 Aug 2016, 'How Joseph Schooling and tiny Singapore rocked Rio'
Wikipedia: Joseph Schooling

facts.text: He won bronze in the 100 m butterfly at the World Championships in Kazan.

sources.label: Wikimedia Commons: Kazan 2015 victory ceremony, 100 m butterfly
ESPN (Julian Linden), 14 Aug 2016, 'How Joseph Schooling and tiny Singapore rocked Rio'

facts.text: On 12 Aug 2016 in Rio he won the 100 m butterfly in an Olympic record 50.39; Phelps, Chad le Clos and Laszlo Cseh tied for silver.

sources.label: ESPN (Julian Linden), 14 Aug 2016, 'How Joseph Schooling and tiny Singapore rocked Rio'
Wikipedia: Joseph Schooling

facts.text: Colin, unwell, stayed in Singapore and watched at the home of Joseph's friend Teo Zhen Ren.
facts.quote: I love you. Son, you have done the nation very proud.
facts.speaker: Colin Schooling, his first words to his son

sources.label: The Sunday Times (May Chen), 14 Aug 2016, 'A seven-year struggle to Olympic glory' (reprint)

facts.text: In the stands, May did not even notice the three-way tie for second.
facts.quote: He's done it! He's done it!
facts.speaker: May Schooling, remembering the moment

sources.label: Singapore Women's Weekly, interview with May Schooling

facts.text: On the victory lap he told Phelps 'Dude, this is crazy'; Phelps patted his back and said 'I know.'
facts.quote: I'm so proud of Joe
facts.speaker: Michael Phelps

sources.label: The Sunday Times (May Chen, Rio), 14 Aug 2016, 'His first steps as Olympic victor' (reprint)

facts.text: He described his career so far as breaking through a wall.
facts.quote: For the first guy through the wall, it's always bloody and I had to take that blow
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling

sources.label: ESPN (Julian Linden), 14 Aug 2016, 'How Joseph Schooling and tiny Singapore rocked Rio'
The Sunday Times (May Chen, Rio), 14 Aug 2016, 'His first steps as Olympic victor' (reprint)

facts.text: At dawn the next morning he had breakfast alone with headphones on, watching the sunrise from the dining hall.
facts.quote: My life will never be the same again.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling

sources.label: SwimSwam Magazine, 2025, 'Joseph Schooling: Singapore's hero'

facts.text: He flew home for an open-top bus parade through crowds (18 Aug 2016) and received S$1 million under the Multi-Million Dollar Award Programme, 20% of it returned to the swimming association.

sources.label: ESPN (Julian Linden), 14 Aug 2016, 'How Joseph Schooling and tiny Singapore rocked Rio'
Prestige Singapore, 2 Apr 2024, retirement press conference
Wikipedia: Joseph Schooling

facts.text: From August to December 2016 he says fame overwhelmed him; he did not get back in the pool until December, which made Eddie Reese nervous.
facts.quote: I kind of lost myself
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling (The New Paper, 2017)

sources.label: SwimSwam, Jun 2017, citing The New Paper interview

facts.text: That autumn he tore his bicep twice; he later said he should have sat out the season.

sources.label: SwimSwam, 2020, on Sergio Lopez podcast

facts.text: An orchid hybrid, Dendrobium Joseph Schooling, was named after him on 7 Aug 2017.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Joseph Schooling
ESPN, 30 Mar 2020, 'Is Joseph Schooling ready for more gold?'

facts.text: After the 2017 worlds he put on about 7 kg and faced public abuse about his weight; he graduated in economics in December 2018 and finished 24th in the 100 m butterfly at the 2019 worlds.
facts.quote: Look, everything crashed in 2019.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling

sources.label: ESPN, 30 Mar 2020, 'Is Joseph Schooling ready for more gold?'

facts.text: Phelps asked him a question he could not answer at first: did he swim for the people in the stands, or for himself?
facts.quote: Why do you swim?
facts.speaker: Michael Phelps, as Schooling recalls

sources.label: ESPN, 30 Mar 2020, 'Is Joseph Schooling ready for more gold?'

facts.text: In February 2020 he moved to Christiansburg, Virginia, to train with Sergio Lopez again; he was recognised there only once, at a Chipotle.

sources.label: ESPN, 30 Mar 2020, 'Is Joseph Schooling ready for more gold?'
SwimSwam, 2020, on Sergio Lopez podcast

facts.text: At the Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021) he went out in the heats of the 100 m butterfly.

sources.label: AP via ESPN, 31 Aug 2022
Reuters via ESPN, 2 Apr 2024

facts.text: Colin died of cancer on 18 Nov 2021, aged 73; Joseph posted a childhood photo of the two of them with only a heart.
facts.quote: It is hard to say goodbye, so let's begin with 'see you again'.
facts.speaker: May Schooling

sources.label: Tatler Asia, 'Joseph Schooling's father Colin dies aged 73' (Nov 2021)
Prestige Singapore, 2 Apr 2024, retirement press conference

facts.text: In August 2022 the defence ministry said he had admitted using cannabis overseas in May while on leave for the SEA Games; he apologised.
facts.quote: I gave in to a moment of weakness after going through a very tough period of my life.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling

sources.label: AP via ESPN, 31 Aug 2022
Prestige Singapore, 2 Apr 2024, retirement press conference

facts.text: He announced his retirement at 28 on 2 April 2024 and spoke to reporters at the Chinese Swimming Club.
facts.quote: I woke up not feeling the same excitement to go to practice.
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling

sources.label: Prestige Singapore, 2 Apr 2024, retirement press conference
Reuters via ESPN, 2 Apr 2024

facts.text: He remembered being four, 'hopping into the unreasonably freezing pool'.

sources.label: Prestige Singapore, 2 Apr 2024, retirement press conference

facts.text: His mother's open letter noted that he had moved into his late father's office.
facts.quote: You never lose! You either WIN or LEARN!
facts.speaker: May Schooling

sources.label: May Schooling's letter, first published in The Straits Times, via Women's Weekly (Apr 2024)

facts.text: He now works in venture capital, plays golf and runs a swim school that teaches water safety.
facts.quote: I want to teach water safety
facts.speaker: Joseph Schooling (SwimSwam, 2025)

sources.label: Prestige Singapore, 2 Apr 2024, retirement press conference
SwimSwam Magazine, 2025, 'Joseph Schooling: Singapore's hero'
